content: fitzgen removed the review request for wasmtime-compiler-reviewers from PR #15048.

fitzgen opened PR #15048 from fitzgen:enums-in-for-each-vm-type-macro to bytecodealliance:main:

Needed for upcoming work to transfer borrows to their owner inline in adapters, rather than calling out to the host.

alexcrichton commented on PR #15048:

Personally I'll admit I basically have no idea any more what's going on in these macros, they're far beyond what I can keep in my head. Otherwise though can you detail a bit more about how the enum bits are integrated? For example how do alias regions work out? While structs can have a separate region-per-field with the nature of aliasing enums and being union-like I'd naively expect such aliasing to be much trickier with a perhaps temporary fallback of "one region per enum", but even then I'm not sure how struct-in-enum would interact since regions could then start overlapping.

Otherwise I'll also note that I've been historically surprised by the layout of #[repr(C)] enums in Rust. Layouts of them are surprisingly subtle and I've gotten it wrong in the C API when trying to mirror the Rust structures into C headers before. I don't understand enum layout enough really to know what went wrong, nor do I understand the macros enough to know if it would match up to rustc's layout, but I mostly wanted to point out that platforms are really weird in the full breadth of things and enums that works on one platform may not always work the same on others.

fitzgen commented on PR #15048:

I don't know about any weird platform gotchas -- you would know about those better than me. FWIW, the macro-generated layout tests are passing everywhere we run them in CI. We could always manually define a struct { tag, union } to avoid supporting enums in this macro, but my understanding is that this is actually identical to what repr(C) on an enum does (correct me if I'm wrong!).

Right now it is generating a separate region per variant field, which is valid for the use cases I currently have that never change enum variants while Wasm code has access to the enum, but I think you are right that doing so could cause problems down the line. So conservatively using one region per enum (or one for the tag and one for the data) at least for now seems like a good idea.

alexcrichton commented on PR #15048:

Reading over the Rust RFC for this I think I remember my historical confusion in the C API. Specifically #[repr(u8)] and #[repr(C, u8)] have entirely different layouts and I was historically not expecting that.

Re-reading that RFC I think it might be good to require #[repr(C, uNN)] here instead of just #[repr(C)] to explicitly say how big the tag is as opposed to using whatever the platform default is as that's pretty nebulous. Alternatively #[repr(uN)] could be used for the slight space savings if any of the enums being added actually benefit from it.

fitzgen commented on PR #15048:

Re-reading that RFC I think it might be good to require #[repr(C, uNN)] here instead of just #[repr(C)] to explicitly say how big the tag is as opposed to using whatever the platform default is as that's pretty nebulous. Alternatively #[repr(uN)] could be used for the slight space savings if any of the enums being added actually benefit from it.

Yep, we do force repr(C, uNN) with an explicit uNN, instead of allowing plain repr(C): https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/pull/15048/changes#diff-c2419e7dda6ababddf61ec427594de45d7710ed2e501264d8fd754635daaa7a8R1047
